q1_issues.issue: The party tag "R-" is expanded into (Past (Member frist republican)); the instruction set states that a party/district tag has no licensed head and must be left out with the gap recorded.
The district tag "Tenn." is turned into (Past (From frist tennessee)) — a From origin relation the sentence never states (no "from" appears in the text), asserted from the same barred tag.
(Name tennessee "Tenn.") invents a proper-noun referent out of the district tag, and its Name string does not even match the symbol derived for it.

q2_gaps: Party/district tags ("R-Tenn.", "D-Ashford") — the instruction set registers that these have no licensed head, so the affiliation stated in the sentence cannot be encoded at all.

An adjective with a finite clausal complement ("confident (that) P") — the complements section covers only an adjective's PP complement; attaching the sealed proposition by Theme on the reified state witness is an unspecified extension.
First-person pronouns inside a direct quotation ("I" = the quoted speaker, "we" = a speaker-inclusive group) are not covered by the pronoun table, which handles only he/she/they/it.
notes: The quotation itself is handled well: say takes Experiencer with the quote sealed under Theme, "I" resolves to frist, the indefinite "a bill" correctly stays inside the seal while the Name projects, and "absolutely" becomes a surface-lemma Degree beside the asserted positive. The R-Tenn. expansion is the substantive defect — three atoms asserted from a tag the instruction set explicitly bars.
